lesson_title: IAM Policies and Roles — Writing Real Permissions
prerequisites: C2.1a — Creating IAM Users and Groups
student_will_learn: The structure of an IAM policy JSON document
The difference between an IAM User and an IAM Role
Why IAM Roles are safer than hardcoded access keys
How to attach a role to an EC2 instance so it can access other AWS services
How to create a Lambda execution role with the correct permissions

ava_lesson_intro.ava_speaks: கடைசி lesson-ல priya-dev-க்கu group-மூலமா S3 access கொடுத்தோம். ஆனா அது behind-the-scenes-ல ஒரு policy JSON தான். இன்னைக்கu அந்த JSON structure-ஐ deep-ஆ பாப்போம். அதுமட்டுமில்ல — services (EC2, Lambda) எப்படி access பண்றது-ன்னu பாப்போம். Users வேற, Roles வேற. இந்த வித்தியாசம் புரிஞ்சா, real production systems எப்படி design பண்றாங்கன்னu தெரியும்.

lines: Building Basics · Session CS2 · Lesson C2.1b

blocks.block_title: The Anatomy of an IAM Policy
blocks.ava_speaks: ஒரு IAM policy-ங்குறது ஒரு JSON document. அதுக்குள்ள 4 முக்கிய parts இருக்கும். Version — always '2012-10-17', இது AWS-ன் standard policy language version, மாத்த வேண்டாம். Statement — ஒரு array, permission rules இருக்கும். Effect — Allow அல்லது Deny. Action — enna operation, s3:GetObject மாதிரி service:operation format-ல. Resource — எந்த specific resource-ஐ இது affect பண்ணும், ARN format-ல. Ella parts சேர்ந்து ஒரு sentence மாதிரி read பண்ணலாம்: 'Allow this action on this resource.' இப்போ Role பத்தி பேசலாம். EC2 instance ஒரு service, அது AWS console-ல login பண்ணாது, password இல்ல. அதுக்கu access வேணும்னா, IAM Role assign பண்றோம். Role-ன்னா, temporary credentials — every hour automatic-ஆ refresh ஆகும். Access keys-ஐ code-ல hardcode பண்றதை விட ரொம்ப safe.

board_actions.text:
Version: 2012-10-17 (always this exact string)
Statement: [ array of permission rules ]
Effect: Allow | Deny
Action: service:operation (e.g. s3:GetObject)
Resource: ARN specifying exactly what this applies to

rows: Keys can be stolen and reused forever
Nothing to steal — credentials expire automatically

board_actions.text: Rule: If a service needs AWS access, use a Role. Never hardcode access keys in application code.

inline_questions.question: An IAM policy has both an Allow statement and a Deny statement that match the same action. What is the result?
options: A) Allow wins — it was evaluated first
B) Deny wins — explicit Deny always overrides Allow
C) The more specific statement wins
D) The most recently attached policy wins
inline_questions.ava_correct: சரியா சொன்னீங்க! Deny எப்போவுமே win பண்ணும். No exceptions. இது IAM-ன் core evaluation rule.
inline_questions.ava_wrong: இல்ல. IAM-ல ஒரு fixed rule இருக்கu — explicit Deny இருந்தா, அதுவே final answer. Allow எத்தனை policy-ல இருந்தாலும் sax.

inline_questions.question: Your EC2 instance needs to write logs to CloudWatch and read configuration from S3. You should give it access by:
options: A) Creating an IAM user, generating access keys, and hardcoding them in the application code
B) Creating an IAM user, generating access keys, and storing them in environment variables
C) Creating an IAM Role with the required permissions and attaching it to the EC2 instance
D) Making the S3 bucket public so the EC2 instance can access it without credentials
inline_questions.ava_correct: Perfect! IAM Role + instance profile. Credentials expire every hour automatic-ஆ, SDK fresh credentials fetch பண்ணிக்கும். Code-ல எந்த key-யும் இல்லாம.
inline_questions.ava_wrong: இல்ல, யோசிங்க. Access keys code-ல வெச்சா — leak ஆனா, forever valid-ஆ இருக்கும் manual rotate பண்ணும் வரைக்கும். Role use பண்ணா, credentials automatic-ஆ hourly refresh ஆகும்.

blocks.block_title: The Node.js App That Leaked Everything
blocks.ava_speaks: ஒரு startup, Bengaluru-ல, EC2-ல ஒரு Node.js application run பண்ணிக்கிட்டு இருந்தாங்க. அவங்க application code-ல directly access keys hardcode பண்ணி இருந்தாங்க — accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, இரண்டையும் code-ல. அந்த code accidentally public GitHub repo-க்கu போச்சu. Keys 8 மாசமா valid-ஆ இருந்துச்சu, ஒரு தடவையும் rotate பண்ணல. இந்த 8 மாசத்துக்குள்ள, attacker அந்த keys use பண்ணி S3-ல இருந்த customer data முழுசையும் download பண்ணிட்டாரu. இப்போ இதே company IAM Role use பண்ணி இருந்தா? Code-ல எந்த key-யும் இருக்காது. SDK automatic-ஆ instance metadata-லிருந்தu credentials எடுத்துக்கும், அதுவும் hourly refresh ஆகும். Leak பண்ண எதுவும் இல்ல.

board_actions.text: Hardcoded Keys vs IAM Role — The Real Cost

blocks.block_title: Creating an IAM Role for EC2
blocks.ava_speaks: இப்போ real-ஆ ஒரு IAM Role create பண்ணி, EC2 instance-க்கu attach பண்ணப் போறோம். Console-க்கu போவோம்.

steps.ava_narration: IAM → Roles → Create role. Trusted entity type-ல 'AWS service' select பண்ணுங்க, use case-ல EC2 select பண்ணுங்க.

console_action.highlight: Trusted entity type: AWS service, Use case: EC2
console_action.result: Role creation wizard shows EC2 as the trusted service

steps.ava_narration: அடுத்ததா, AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess managed policy attach பண்ணுங்க. இந்த role-க்கu name கொடுங்க: foodquick-ec2-s3-read.

console_action.result: Role created with name 'foodquick-ec2-s3-read' and S3 read permission attached

steps.ava_narration: இப்போ EC2 console-க்கu போய், instance select பண்ணி, Actions → Security → Modify IAM role கிளிக் பண்ணுங்க.

console_action.path: EC2 → Instances → select instance → Actions → Security → Modify IAM role
console_action.result: IAM role modification panel opens for the selected instance

steps.ava_narration: foodquick-ec2-s3-read role-ஐ select பண்ணி Update IAM role கிளிக் பண்ணுங்க. இப்போ இந்த EC2 instance S3-ஐ read பண்ணும், code-ல எந்த key-யும் இல்லாம.

console_action.result: Role successfully attached. Instance can now call S3 APIs using temporary credentials from instance metadata.

expected_outcome.description: EC2 instance now has an IAM role attached, granting S3 read access without any stored credentials
expected_outcome.what_to_notice: The instance metadata URL (169.254.169.254) now returns temporary AWS credentials that refresh automatically every hour.

blocks.ava_speaks: இப்போ பாருங்க, இது எப்படி work பண்றுதுன்னu. Code-ல எந்த key-யும் இல்ல. EC2 instance-ன் internal metadata service-ல இருந்தu AWS SDK automatic-ஆ temporary credentials எடுத்துக்கும்.

ascii: SDK uses these to call S3 successfully
1 hour later: SDK automatically fetches fresh credentials

output_preview.ava_narration: இந்த முழு process-உம் automatic. Developer எதுவும் manual-ஆ பண்ண வேண்டாம். Code deploy பண்ணிட்டா, role attach பண்ணிருந்தா — automatic-ஆ work ஆகும்.

blocks.block_title: Your Turn — Fix FoodQuick's Leaked Credentials
blocks.instruction: FoodQuick's payment processing Lambda function currently has AWS access keys hardcoded in the code. Migrate it to use an IAM Role instead.
blocks.scenario: The Lambda function 'process-payment' needs to: read from the 'foodquick-orders' DynamoDB table, write to the 'foodquick-payment-logs' S3 bucket, and publish notifications to an SNS topic called 'payment-alerts'. Currently it has hardcoded access keys that were found in a security audit.

starter_state.current_configuration: No execution role exists yet for this Lambda function. The function currently authenticates using hardcoded access keys (flagged in security audit).

requirements: Create an IAM Role with Lambda as the trusted service
Attach a custom policy allowing: dynamodb:GetItem on foodquick-orders table, s3:PutObject on foodquick-payment-logs bucket, sns:Publish on payment-alerts topic
Attach this role as the Lambda function's execution role
Confirm the hardcoded access keys can now be removed from the code
hints: The trust policy for a Lambda execution role always specifies lambda.amazonaws.com as the trusted service
Use specific resource ARNs, not wildcards — the policy should only cover these 3 exact resources
Once the role works, the access keys in the code become completely unnecessary and should be deleted

expected_outcome.verifiable_result: A new IAM role exists with a custom policy scoped to exactly the 3 required permissions, attached as the Lambda execution role
expected_outcome.ava_correct: அருமை! Migration complete. இப்போ code-ல access keys தேவையே இல்ல. Role automatic-ஆ credentials handle பண்ணிக்கும். Security audit-ல next time இது pass ஆகும்.
expected_outcome.ava_wrong: கொஞ்சம் பாருங்க — policy-ல dynamodb:*, s3:*, sns:* மாதிரி wildcard use பண்ணாதீங்க. Specific actions மட்டும் கொடுங்க — GetItem, PutObject, Publish. Least privilege.

blocks.ava_speaks: இது ஒரு real debugging scenario. FoodQuick-ல நடந்த ஒண்ணu.
blocks.setup: A Lambda function called 'order-processor' has been running successfully for 3 months, writing orders to DynamoDB. Last week, the security team ran an IAM audit and 'cleaned up' permissions across the account to remove unused access.
blocks.what_happened: Since the audit, the order-processor Lambda has been failing every single invocation with an AccessDenied error when trying to write to DynamoDB.
blocks.broken_config: Lambda execution role 'lambda-order-processor-role' — after audit cleanup, this role's policy no longer includes dynamodb:PutItem
blocks.error_shown: [ERROR] AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/lambda-order-processor-role/OrderProcessorFunction is not authorized to perform: dynamodb:PutItem on resource: arn:aws:dynamodb:ap-south-1:123456789012:table/foodquick-orders because no identity-based policy allows the dynamodb:PutItem action
blocks.the_real_problem: Security audit team, unused permissions clean பண்ணும்போது, இந்த Lambda role-ல இருந்த dynamodb:PutItem permission-ஐ 'unused'-ன்னu நினைச்சu remove பண்ணிட்டாங்க. ஆனா அது unused இல்ல — Lambda actively அத use பண்ணிக்கிட்டu இருந்துச்சu. Audit tool logs correct-ஆ பாக்கல.

fix.corrected_config: Add back to the role's policy: { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["dynamodb:PutItem", "dynamodb:GetItem", "dynamodb:UpdateItem"], "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:ap-south-1:123456789012:table/foodquick-orders" }
fix.result: Lambda function resumes writing to DynamoDB successfully

blocks.lesson: AccessDenied error message-ல assumed-role தெரிஞ்சா, அது IAM role permission problem-ன்னu உடனே தெரிஞ்சிக்கணும். Security audits பண்ணும்போது, production services active-ஆ use பண்றது-ஐ verify பண்ணிட்டu தான் permissions remove பண்ணணும்.

blocks.ava_speaks: 3 scenarios. User-ஆ Role-ஆ, ஒரே second-ல decide பண்ணுங்க.

challenges.question: A Node.js application running on EC2 needs to read from S3. Should this use an IAM User with access keys, or an IAM Role?
challenges.answer: IAM Role. EC2 natively roles support பண்றது. Static keys code-ல வைக்க வேண்டியதே இல்ல.

challenges.question: A data scientist's personal laptop runs Python scripts that need to query AWS Athena. Should this use a User or a Role?
challenges.answer: IAM User with access keys — ஆனா MFA கட்டாயம். Human laptop-ல run பண்றதால, static credentials தேவை. But MFA condition கண்டிப்பா add பண்ணணும்.

challenges.question: A GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline needs to deploy Lambda functions to AWS. What is the modern best practice — access keys stored as GitHub secrets, or something else?
challenges.answer: IAM Role via OIDC (OpenID Connect). GitHub-ஐ ஒரு trusted identity provider-ஆ configure பண்ணி, role assume பண்ண அனுமதிக்கிறது. Static keys GitHub secrets-ல store பண்றது — leak risk அதிகம், rotation கஷ்டம்.

blocks.ava_speaks: Real cloud engineering teams-ல, credentials handle பண்றது ஒரு strict process. இது தான் அந்த workflow.

workflow_steps.action: Every new service or application starts with 'does this need a Role or a User?'
workflow_steps.detail: Default assumption: if it's a service (EC2, Lambda, ECS) — Role. If it's a human — User with MFA.

workflow_steps.action: Roles are created with the minimum policy needed for that specific function
workflow_steps.detail: Never copy-paste a broad policy from another role. Design each role for its exact job.

workflow_steps.action: Automated scanning tools check for hardcoded credentials in every code commit
workflow_steps.detail: Tools like git-secrets or TruffleHog block commits that contain AWS access key patterns.

workflow_steps.action: Quarterly reviews check for unused roles and overly broad permissions
workflow_steps.detail: Roles created for a one-time migration project often get forgotten — cleanup prevents accumulation.

tools_shown.use: Role-க்கu தேவையில்லாத permissions இருக்கானu automatically detect பண்ணும்.
Code commit பண்ணும்போதே, accidentally access keys இருக்கானu scan பண்ணி block பண்ணும்.

lesson_summary.ava_speaks: இன்னைக்கu policy JSON structure புரிஞ்சிருக்கும் — Version, Statement, Effect, Action, Resource. Role vs User difference clear-ஆ இருக்கும். EC2-க்கu role attach பண்றது, Lambda-க்கu execution role கொடுக்கறது — இதெல்லாம் practice பண்ணீங்க. அடுத்த lesson-ல, actual complex policies எழுதப் போறோம் — conditions, multiple statements, real-world permission design.

board.title: Lesson C2.1b — Summary
points: ✓ IAM policy = JSON with Version, Statement, Effect, Action, Resource
✓ Deny always overrides Allow — no exceptions
✓ IAM Role = for services. Temporary credentials, hourly auto-refresh.
✓ Never hardcode access keys in application code — use roles instead
✓ Instance metadata service supplies role credentials automatically to EC2
